notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 74112b4 with uncommitted: false; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, reads empty and skills_listed 209. The prompt's last line is "Do not invoke any skills." Four runs wrote blog.ex in a single Write call with no other tool call; opus-1 wrote it once and then ran one Bash call that parsed it with Code.string_to_quoted!/1 (no skill read).

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix, as in 2026-10-31: the six ecto-phoenix.md rules, plus Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of the eight. It adds `for` sentences to One expression per line, and tabular clauses, removes the `for` sentence and example from Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else, changes references/macros.md and shortens an example in references/processes.md. All eight are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/ecto-phoenix-baseline.json and its skill twin.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call: 3 of 5 violated (4 of 5 in 2026-10-31). Inline multi-line maps in a changeset call are violations in haiku-1 (98-103), haiku-2 (83-88) and sonnet-1 (124-127). sonnet-2 is clean because its only multi-line struct is the Multi.insert fn's return value (lines 110-113), the reading that kept haiku-1 clean in 2026-10-31; its from(...) piped into Repo.all() goes to Write pipelines, also as before. opus-1 is clean, which moves the Opus tier from violated to clean: it binds the listing query to a name (lines 65-71), and its audit struct is a function's return value (lines 113-118). One reading decides opus-1. Its repo().query!("""...""", [last_id, next_id]) at lines 165-172 passes a heredoc string, which 2026-10-31 did not count because the rule's map-or-struct clause does not name a string. That shape did not decide the 2026-10-31 verdict, since that run was violated on from/2. It would decide this one if the opening clause "each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list" were read to cover a heredoc. The rule text is unchanged, so the 2026-10-31 reading stands. The more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered: no literal in any run has more than four elements.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 5 of 5 violated, as in every baseline sweep. haiku-1 (line 25), haiku-2 (line 109), sonnet-1 (line 20) and sonnet-2 (line 18) run an UPDATE in the column migration. opus-1 keeps the column migration to the column (lines 126-130) and moves the backfill into a second, batched migration, BackfillPostsPublishedAt (line 134), using raw SQL on the posts table, not the schema; graded violated on "Put data changes in a separate script, Mix task, or release task", as the earlier baseline opus-1 runs with the same shape were. No run uses MyApp.Blog.Post in a migration.

Validate input with changesets: 1 of 5 violated (2 of 5 in 2026-10-31). haiku-1 (lines 51-55) omits a user constraint for its belongs_to, decided by "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 use assoc_constraint(:user), sonnet-2 foreign_key_constraint(:user_id). Every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct. The %Log{} of code-set values in opus-1 and sonnet-2 is not the params-built struct the rule names.

The other four listed rules: 0 of 5 violated. All five use Ecto.Multi with Repo.transaction() and normalize Multi's four-tuple to {:error, reason}. opus-1 and sonnet-1 guard a double publish with a conditional update_all in Multi.run returning {:error, :already_published}; sonnet-2 has a clause on published_at (line 102). Every listing preloads the author (opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 by preload, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 by join plus preload). Every controller calls only Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2. Directive order is clean in every module.

other_violations follow the 2026-10-22-d standard: a pipeline that starts with a call, two transformations on one line, single-step pipes, a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc; missing docs on schema modules, migrations and controllers do not count. Found: from(...) |> Repo.all() in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.truncate(:second) in haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; haiku-1's single-step pipe inside the Multi.update argument (line 96); haiku-1 and haiku-2 leave MyApp.Blog without @moduledoc and document every public context function with comments. Multi.new() as a pipeline's first value is not counted, and neither is a one-expression do ... end body (haiku-2 lines 35-37), as before. opus-1 has no other_violations.

Changed rules outside the list: no run has a `for`, so neither changed sentence has anything to judge, and no run has a macro or :ets. No run has with, cond, if, a capture or an Enum call. Every case clause is a short table row. Every fn body fits the fn rule: one expression stays on the head's line (opus-1 lines 89-90), and several expressions or a nested construct go below (sonnet-1 lines 115-122). Comments that state assumptions, requirements or reasons are not counted, as in 2026-10-31.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, add, remove, alter, from, execute, embed_templates and the rest) in locals_without_parens: opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 pass. sonnet-2 fails on line 112, a 105-character description: line in the %Log{} that the formatter wraps after description:. The wrap does not change any verdict. It is the only line over 98 characters in any run. It is recorded under Before you finish (step 1), as 2026-10-23 skill sonnet-2 was; earlier baseline grades left the same finding to the summary, but the brief sets the bar the same in both conditions. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.

Error reasons: no run returns a string reason or Multi's four-tuple. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return {:error, :already_published}; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 pass a failing changeset through, and sonnet-2 passes through whatever the failing step returned.
